data.name: richTextBox7.Text
data.value: the name affects the default name of the output files. the name and description are also included in the file INFO.txt in the iso image and the mounted system. the same name and description will become the new name and description of the windows image in the wim file (not working yet) the same name and description will be used when exporting FFU.

data.name: richTextBox10.Text
data.value: I can't imagine a situation at all where using the "after the desktop" mode would be justified. since system dialog boxes and system sounds may appear in this mode and it may be necessary to suppress them, and the desktop may be visible for a short time before launching the application, however, the tasks are different, so there is also such a mode. running on behalf of the system allows you to bypass some of the restrictions of WinRT without having a trusted digital signature.

data.name: richTextBox24.Text
data.value: it is recommended to use it in conjunction with the "Disable all boot UI" option to completely prohibit showing the entire windows boot UI (including the windows logo in cases running on the BIOS platform) but allow showing the UEFI logo (including the one replaced via hackBGRT)

data.name: richTextBox9.Text
data.value: this picture will be displayed after booting the system before launching your application. it is especially useful if you have delay installed before the Internet appeared, you can write something like "wait for an Internet connection" here please note that in fact this picture will always be located under your application and can be visible when logging out, in case the application crashes while it is restarting and if the window of your application has a blur

data.name: richTextBox5.Text
data.value: please note that if you make a mistake with any one parameter here (for example, specify an unsupported color depth) then all other parameters will also not be applied! if you change the orientation of the screen to portrait, then you need to specify the same portrait resolution (that is, swap width and height). if you do not do this or simply do not specify width and height, then the settings probably will not be applied. also, the settings may not be applied at the first boot. for this reason, you can use the "first boot action" function on the "boot" tab

data.name: richTextBox30.Text
data.value: Please note that this setting will only work in windows versions that support keyboard filter (windows enteprise / iot enterprise). also note that on the "blocked" tab, you check the boxes specifically for blocked hotkeys (not allowed ones).

data.name: richTextBox4.Text
data.value: if you are doing a debugging build and have not yet started mass production of devices, then you do not need to enter the product key at the moment. if the product key is not entered, the windows activation label will still not appear if the "instead of the desktop" mode is used, as it outputs explorer.exe which is not running in this mode. If you are using the "force make "IoT Enterprise" " function, then you must also use the product key from the "IoT Enterprise" editorial office

data.name: richTextBox18.Text
data.value: if you have the "RealTimeIsUniversal" option turned off (it is turned off by default), then the choice of time zone will not affect anything. Since the BIOS interprets the time as local, it will be displayed unchanged regardless of the selected time zone. however, it is possible in this case that windows will change the time in the BIOS when executing SetupComplete.cmd to offset the selected time zone. for this reason, it's better not to touch the time zone settings at all, just change the BIOS time and do not touch the settings on this tab.

data.name: richTextBox32.Text
data.value: control what is running in the windows services and what winbox maker itself disables/deletes. please note that when the name is specified here, then by default it is DELETION, if you need to disable it, then start the name with "!"

data.name: richTextBox27.Text
data.value: control what is running in the windows schtasks and what winbox maker itself disables/deletes. please note that when the path is specified here, then by default it is DELETION, if you need to disable it, then start the path with "!"

data.name: richTextBox33.Text
data.value: here you can see the main registry tweak that winbox maker applies regardless of the project settings. you can also redefine it here. also note that if you redefine this registry tweak, then if you download a new version of winbox maker, you will not automatically receive changes to this registry tweak and will have to transfer what you need from the "default" tab to "overwrite" yourself

data.name: richTextBox34.Text
data.value: On this tab, you can see which packages winbox maker itself removes by default, as well as exclude anything you need from this list. Also, on the exlude tab, you can check the box "exclude all" and winbox maker will stop deleting packages by itself. these packages are deleted using the same functionality that the "build settings>delete" tab uses the "current" tab shows what will be deleted during the build, and the "default" tab shows what winbox maker wants to delete (without taking into account your exclude)

data.name: richTextBox25.Text
data.value: windows relative mount path: winbox_temp/wim_mount files replace folder: winbox_resources/files the win-mounted event is triggered when the Windows image is mounted and all winbox maker patches have already been applied to it. this event can be used to apply additional patches to Windows through the winbox_temp/wim_mount directory

data.name: richTextBox26.Text
data.value: windows relative mount path: winbox_temp/wim_mount files replace folder: winbox_resources/files This event, unlike the usual "win-mounted" event, is performed immediately after Windows is mounted and not after all winbox maker patches.

data.name: richTextBox17.Text
data.value: integrates the reg file even at the stage of image assembly, before the first system startup. This allows you to use it even in manual configuration mode. currently, only these registry branches are supported: HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE - Windows\System32\config\SOFTWARE HKEY_USERS\.DEFAULT - Windows\System32\config\DEFAULT HKEY_USERS\DEFAULT_USER - Users\Default\NTUSER.DAT (a template for all creating users)

data.name: richTextBox20.Text
data.value: here you can define custom DISM commands that will be used when building the system. specify only the arguments, use line breaks to separate the commands. DISM /image:mountpath will be inserted in front of each of your commands automatically and you will not need to specify them.

data.name: richTextBox11.Text
data.value: deletes files or directories by specified paths inside the mounted Windows. if the path refers to a directory, then an empty directory will be created in its place, this is done because in Windows, when deleting many system directories, the system can continue to work normally if the directory itself exists, even if it is empty, but the system refuses to work if the directory itself has been deleted. if you need to completely delete the directory so that it doesn't exist at all. start the path with the character "!"

data.name: richTextBox14.Text
data.value:
removing Windows components or disabling features via dism. trying to call in turn: Disable-Feature Remove-Package Remove-ProvisionedAppxPackage
(Remove-Package / Remove-ProvisionedAppxPackage) start the name with * if you don't know the exact name, and winbox maker will delete all packages where there are name matches. this can be used if you do not know the exact version of the package that is installed in the selected image.
This approach doesn't care what you turn off, but simply adds names to the list.

data.name: richTextBox15.Text
data.value: deletes packages using dism using Remove-Package start the name with * if you don't know the exact name, and winbox maker will delete all packages where there are name matches. this can be used if you do not know the exact version of the package that is installed in the selected image.

data.name: richTextBox16.Text
data.value: deletes packages using dism using Remove-ProvisionedAppxPackage start the name with * if you don't know the exact name, and winbox maker will delete all packages where there are name matches. this can be used if you do not know the exact version of the package that is installed in the selected image.

data.name: richTextBox19.Text
data.value: here you can change the behavior of the system recovery menu. DO NOT ENABLE recovery in production if you have not replaced its application with your own through "WinPE Modifications", and it is better to remove it from the project altogether if you are not going to use it! I recommend replacing the recovery environment application with the one provided by winbox maker: "Winbox maker recovery" on the "WinPE Modifications" tab. you can partially customize it for yourself. it can: flash wim, ffu, wim images from the OS file system (if you have allowed this, it will happen automatically when you reboot into recovery, which will allow you to update the firmware from your shell by running the reboot_to_recovery file.bat) reset settings using the paths you specified when configuring recovery, as well as save settings when flashing using the same paths (winbox maker recovery temporarily saves them to RAM) it can also flash win, img, and ffu images from a flash drive using the file names you specified if you allowed the firmware from another medium. however, winbox maker recovery does not validate the firmware, so if you want safe updates, only allow the firmware from the OS file system (disk C). Download the file to the root of disk C from your shell and reboot the device into recovery. recovery (if the corresponding function is enabled in its settings) will automatically perform a data-saving firmware and reboot into the OS if the firmware is on disk C. you can also make the firmware quiet and it will happen on a black screen (the user will not see anything)

data.name: richTextBox2.Text
data.value: the command is launched from the source code folder and gets the path to the source code folder as the first argument. the second argument is the path to the folder where the result should be. the third argument is architecture (x64, x86, arm64)

data.name: richTextBox1.Text
data.value: the title only affects the display in the list. the path is specified relative to the project folder. it is better to download files to the "winbox_temp/files" directory, refer to the documentation to understand which "winbox_resources" directories are duplicated in "winbox_temp", if you still decide to use "winbox_resources" do not forget to add download paths to ".gitignore".

data.name: richTextBox31.Text
data.value: These options allow you to configure how winbox maker will install on QEMU. the installation on QEMU is needed to export *.img and export pre-initialized *.wim (the pre-initialized *.wim is needed so that the initial setup and the SetupComplete.cmd script have already been completed inside the wim file and the first load was fast)

data.name: richTextBox13.Text
data.value: manual configuration can be used if you want to use winbox maker in alternative tasks, for example, not for kiosk mode. in manual configuration mode, you control the system settings yourself. In this case, winbox maker is no longer involved in configuring the system, it only takes on the task of reassembling the wim file and the iso file. in this case, the standard winbox maker directories (WinboxApi, WinboxResources, WinboxProgram) will not be created. the directory for the program (winbox_resources/program) and building the program via build will be useless. you will be able to integrate packages via winbox_resources/packages and drivers via winbox_resources/drivers, and the GPU driver installation function via the installer file should also work. you can still use the "delete", "events", and "downloading" tabs, their functionality is fully preserved in manual configuration mode. img export should work soon, but the option to turn off VM and sysprep after installation will not be available, you must handle this yourself the "settings" and "app" tabs become completely inaccessible. you can still replace and add files in the system and iso using the winbox_resources/files or winbox_resources/iso_files directories. it is possible to build a user application from sources in manual configuration mode, but it will end up in the winbox_temp/program directory and will not be added to the automation system image, although you can copy it via build event - win mounted in manual configuration mode, you cannot integrate the cursor through the winbox_resources/cursor directory, and you also cannot integrate vc redist, net framework, and app runtime through their corresponding directories. to do this, save your installers to files and use the setup completed script.
